content:
📚 Introduction

Imagine being able to visualize your own storybook scene with just a few clicks—where dragons roam desolate peaks or brave explorers uncover wonders in mysterious forests. With the power of AI and a simple user interface, it's now possible to bring your stories to life, one vivid image at a time.

This blog walks you through a project that lets users generate storybook scenes dynamically using Streamlit, OpenAI's image generation API, and Pillow for image handling. Whether you're an educator, a storyteller, or just an imaginative creator, this tool makes it fun and effortless to produce stunning AI-powered illustrations.

🔧 Tools & Technologies Used

  • Python
  • Streamlit – for building the web UI
  • OpenAI API – for generating images from text prompts
  • Pillow (PIL) – for image processing
  • Requests – to retrieve generated images
  • Certifi – to handle secure HTTPS requests

🛠 How It Works

This interactive web app guides users through creating a visual scene based on a story chapter. By choosing a character, setting, emotional tone, and image size, the app constructs a custom prompt and sends it to OpenAI's image generation model.

Here’s how the process flows:

  1. User Inputs: Chapter title, main character, setting, emotion, and image size.
  2. Prompt Generation: These inputs are woven into a descriptive prompt.
  3. Image Request: The prompt is passed to the OpenAI image generation API.
  4. Image Retrieval & Display: The generated image is fetched and displayed in the app.
  5. Download Option: Users can download the image for personal use or to add to their storybook.

🧙‍♂️ The Creative Controls

Users can pick from a rich set of storytelling options:

  • Characters: Dragon, Knight, Explorer, Wizard, and more.
  • Settings: Forests, Castles, Ocean, Space Stations, etc.
  • Emotions: Happy, Melancholy, Courageous, Tense, etc.
  • Image Sizes: 1024x1024, 512x512, or 256x256.

These combinations help evoke specific visual moods, making each scene unique and emotionally resonant.

💻 Core Code Overview

Here’s a breakdown of key parts of the code:

# Prompt construction
full_prompt = f"{chapter_title}: A scene with {character.lower()} in a {setting.lower()} setting, evoking a {emotion.lower()} emotion"

This line dynamically assembles the story prompt based on user choices—one of the most crucial steps to ensure OpenAI generates accurate visuals.

# Image generation
response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size=size)

The generated image URL is retrieved and then downloaded using the requests library.

# Image display and download
st.image(img, caption=f"Generated Scene: {chapter_title}", use_column_width=True)

🎨 Example Use Case

Chapter Title: The Lonely Dragon
Character: Dragon
Setting: Mountain Peak
Emotion: Melancholy
Result: An AI-generated image depicting a solitary dragon atop a snowy peak, conveying deep emotion—perfect for a children's storybook or fantasy tale.

📥 Bonus: Download & Continue

Once a scene is generated, users can:

  • Download the image in PNG format with a single click.
  • Click "Start Next Chapter" to continue the story and generate the next scene.

This makes it perfect for collaborative storytelling or serialized story creation.

🚀 Final Thoughts

With this interactive storybook scene generator, creativity meets technology in a magical way. Whether you're crafting bedtime stories, building a fantasy world, or experimenting with AI storytelling, this project empowers you to visualize your imagination instantly.

Let your stories not just be told—but seen.

🧩 Want to Try It Yourself?

Here’s what you need to do:

  1. Set up a Python environment.
  2. Install dependencies: streamlit, openai, pillow, and requests.
  3. Save your OpenAI API key in a secure apikey.py file.
  4. Run the Streamlit app:
   streamlit run your_script.py

Happy Storytelling! 🐉📖✨

Python Code:

import os
import certifi
import streamlit as st
from openai import OpenAI
from apikey import apikey  # Store your OpenAI key in apikey.py
import requests
from PIL import Image
from io import BytesIO

# Set up the OpenAI API key
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

# Define character, setting, and emotion options
characters = ["Dragon", "Knight", "Explorer", "Young Girl", "Hero", "Villain", "Wizard", "Fox", "Monster"]
settings = ["Mountain Peak", "Forest", "Castle", "Garden", "Ocean", "Battlefield", "Village", "Desert", "Space Station"]
emotions = ["Happy", "Melancholy", "Tense", "Fearful", "Courageous", "Excited", "Curious", "Relaxed", "Wonder"]

# Streamlit UI setup
st.title("Interactive Storybook Creator with Dynamic Scene Generation")
st.write("Create storybook scenes by specifying the chapter, characters, setting, and emotional tone.")

# User input: Chapter title, characters, setting, emotion, and image size
chapter_title = st.text_input("Enter the chapter title:", "The Lonely Dragon")
character = st.selectbox("Select the main character:", characters)
setting = st.selectbox("Select the setting:", settings)
emotion = st.selectbox("Select the emotional tone of the scene:", emotions)
size = st.selectbox("Select image size:", ["1024x1024", "512x512", "256x256"])

if st.button("Generate Scene"):
    # Combine the inputs into a full prompt
    full_prompt = f"{chapter_title}: A scene with {character.lower()} in a {setting.lower()} setting, evoking a {emotion.lower()} emotion"
    st.write(f"Generating image for: '{full_prompt}'")

    # Generate the image
    response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size=size)
    image_url = response.data[0].url

    # Fetch and display the image
    img_response = requests.get(image_url, verify=certifi.where())
    img = Image.open(BytesIO(img_response.content))

    st.image(img, caption=f"Generated Scene: {chapter_title}", use_column_width=True)

    # Provide an option to download the image
    img_bytes = BytesIO()
    img.save(img_bytes, format="PNG")
    img_bytes.seek(0)
    st.download_button(label="Download Image", data=img_bytes, file_name=f"{chapter_title.lower().replace(' ', '_')}.png", mime="image/png")

    # Option to generate the next chapter's scene
    if st.button("Start Next Chapter"):
        st.write("Proceed to the next chapter by adding a new title, characters, setting, and emotion.")
